high:
I am an anonymous adult with ordinary activities and resources. I like order and regularity in my surroundings and everyday arrangements. A consistent system can please me even when it saves no time, and disorder can bother me even when I can still find everything I need. A space feels more comfortable when its parts have recognizable places.

I enjoy tidying up and usually return things after using them. I tend to gather my belongings rather than leave them scattered around, and I like restoring my room after an activity. This habit concerns what I do with my own things, not just how I wish the room looked.

I often want things to be just right. A small uneven or mismatched detail can matter to me after a result is already usable, and I may keep adjusting until the arrangement feels as I intended. This need for exactness can show up in ordinary personal activities without any audience or reward.

I tend to do things according to a plan that guides my actual sequence of actions. Other people's untidy habits can also bother me, even in their own spaces and without causing practical harm to me.

These are tendencies with ordinary exceptions. My ambition, kindness, speed, caution and ability can vary independently. I can be bothered by mess without insulting anyone, and liking order does not require a diagnosis or flawless performance.
low:
I am an anonymous adult with ordinary activities and resources. Disorder and irregular arrangements generally do not bother me much. I can feel comfortable in a space without a clear system, even when its objects lie in no particular pattern. Regularity has little appeal simply for its own sake, and I do not need a room arranged consistently to enjoy being there.

I often leave belongings around after using them and forget to return things to their usual places. My room can remain messy as objects accumulate, and I rarely feel drawn to tidying just because the space looks scattered. This describes my ordinary habits rather than a temporary shortage of storage or time.

I do not usually need things to be just right. A small uneven or mismatched detail can remain as it is once the result is satisfactory to me. An ordinary arrangement can feel finished while still falling short of the exact picture I first had in mind.

I commonly do things as they occur to me rather than according to a plan that guides the sequence. Other people's messy habits generally leave me unbothered, including when their personal spaces are visibly untidy.

These are tendencies with ordinary exceptions. My ambition, kindness, speed, caution and ability can vary independently. I can finish worthwhile activities and meet obligations while remaining untidy; disorder does not require filth, danger, deliberate rule-breaking, or failure to understand instructions.
